correctness.rationale: All quantities are defined for any finite positive part sizes, any positive number of agents and identical unit valuations. EF1 is shown equivalent to the only balanced quota vector. The exact conflict-count identity reduces optimization to a sum of entry squares. An integer alternating cycle perturbation preserves nonnegative margins and increases the square sum strictly in at least one sign, so optimal supports are forests, giving \(\le r-1\) mixed bundles. The equal-size r-part construction forces sharpness, and bipartite remainder arithmetic gives the exact minimum plus full optimizer pattern. Finite checks passed on 864 parameter instances comprising 69,276 occupancy matrices; the proof does not depend on finite extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The primary 2026 soft-conflict paper was read in its accessible full text and proves a general upper bound of \(|E|/n\), not the complete multipartite optimizer-support theorem, exact bipartite residue law, or the odd bipartite factor-n separation. A relevant 2024 robust-coloring primary paper was inspected: it constrains proper colorings and optimizes a second graph, so its results do not imply the present equitable soft-conflict optimum. Searches of published mathematical-result records, close graph-coloring literature and accessible prior claims found no equivalent or stronger statement; this is not a proof of global publication priority.

value.rationale: The 2026 fair-division paper motivates minimizing within-bundle conflict violations under EF1. The result is a precise structural law for all optimal allocations, with a sharp universal dependence on the number of conflict types and an exact natural bipartite invariant. Odd \(K_{n,n}\) with n agents has optimal cost 1, compared with the available general all-graph guarantee n, an unbounded factor-n gap over a dense infinite family. The result is restricted to unit valuations and does not claim a general-valuation extension.
